transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi... yeah, thank you. Um, well, I guess I'm here because I just... I can't stop going back over the same spreadsheets and calculations at work. Again and again. I do bookkeeping, which I actually started right after high school because my aunt knew the office manager and got me an interview. My aunt is so sweet, she actually just got this little golden retriever puppy that is adorable but he chews on absolutely everything—like he completely ruined her good winter boots last week. 

But um, yeah, at work, I end up staying for hours after everyone else leaves. Even when I've already checked all the numbers. Because if I don't do it just one more time, I get this horrible feeling that something really bad is going to happen and it'll be all my fault. Like, yesterday I stayed so late I completely missed my bus, and the transit schedule is just a nightmare right now anyway because of all that water main construction they're doing on 4th street... they've had the right lane closed for like three months now and the traffic just backs up for miles... but yeah, I just can't stop checking the files.
Do you find that certain thoughts, images, or urges keep coming into your mind, even if you don’t want them to, especially when you're at work or thinking about your tasks?

Yeah... yeah, exactly. It’s like, even after I literally just checked the spreadsheet and I know for a fact the numbers match, this thought just keeps jumping into my head that I missed one hidden mistake somewhere, like in payroll or taxes. Which actually reminds me, tax season is coming up and my mom is already stressing out about it because she lost a whole folder of her receipts when they moved last month. They hired these movers who were supposed to be really professional, but they were so careless and they ended up breaking her favorite lamp, the one with the little stained glass shade she got at an antique fair in like, 2018? It was so pretty, and she was devastated. 

But um, what was I saying? Oh, right, the thoughts at work. Yeah, so I just keep thinking that because of some hidden mistake I made, somebody's check won't go through, or the whole firm is gonna get in massive trouble. And I try so hard to just push the thought away, you know? I try to tell myself it's fine, but it comes right back every single time. It’s honestly like I can't even trust my own eyes anymore. Which is funny because my vision is actually perfect, I went to the optometrist in October and he said I have 20/20 vision, though he did say I should probably buy those blue light glasses since I stare at a computer all day... but yeah, the thoughts just don't stop.
When these thoughts come up at work, do you feel driven to perform certain actions or checks repeatedly to try to reduce the anxiety or prevent something bad from happening?

Yeah, exactly. Like I was saying, that's really why I'm here... I just can't stop going back over the same spreadsheets and calculations again and again. I stay at work for hours after everyone leaves, even when I know I already checked them perfectly. I just feel completely driven to do it one more time, because if I don't, I get that overwhelming feeling that something awful is going to happen and it'll be entirely my fault. 

And honestly, staying that late is so creepy anyway because the motion sensor lights in the hallway turn off, and our security guard, Dave, only does his rounds every two hours. Dave is actually retiring next month, they're having a little potluck for him on a Friday. I was thinking of bringing my pasta salad, but mayonnaise goes bad so fast if it's sitting out, you know? My cousin got food poisoning from potato salad at a family picnic once and she was in the hospital for two days. It was terrifying, she had to get IV fluids and everything. 

But, um... wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, the checking. Yeah, I just have to keep doing the calculations. I literally can't leave my desk until I do it enough times to make that horrible anxious feeling stop, so I just keep checking.
When you feel the urge to check your work but you're unable to do so, does it cause you a lot of anxiety or distress?

Oh god, yes. If I can't check it, I feel like I'm going to jump out of my skin. My chest gets all tight and I can't focus on anything else. Like, if my boss calls me into a meeting right when I'm in the middle of double-checking a column, I just sit in the meeting sweating, completely convinced that the file I left open on my desk is wrong and the whole company is going to collapse because of it. 

Our meetings are so long, too. My boss, Mr. Henderson, he loves to hear himself talk. He spent like twenty minutes last week talking about his new golf clubs. He got these custom titanium ones that apparently cost more than my car. Which, honestly, my car has been making this weird rattling noise lately when I go over 40 miles an hour. I took it to the mechanic, this guy Tony who my dad has gone to for years, and he said it was the catalytic converter or something? But the part is backordered for like six weeks because of supply chain issues. It's so frustrating because I really need my car to get to the grocery store on weekends. The one near my apartment is so overpriced, they charge like seven dollars for a regular carton of eggs now. 

But um... yeah. If I can't check the numbers, the panic just builds and builds until I feel like I can't even breathe. I just have to get back to my desk and look at it again.
